title: The Plantation Cafe, the Sunset, the Dreamland glass floor and the Royal Garden
summary: Howard locates the Plantation at 35th and Calumet and discusses Chicago spots, dance floors, the Deluxe and where Oliver opened.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What kind of a place was the Plantation? Oh, it was a fine night spot. That was 64th and Cottage Grove?
No, no, no, that's the Persian Palace. Oh, oh, oh. No, this was 35th and Calumet, right adjacent from the Sunset Cafe. Plantation here, Sunset's on the other corner.
Describe the inside of the place.
Well, they had a big dance floor where they conducted the shows.
Where was the dance floor? In the middle of the? Yes, in the middle.
Most of the Chicago spots, all the dance floors, right from the bandstand. Is that the place where they had a glass?
No, that's Dreamland.
That's the Dreamland. 3520 State. That was Killa.
Well, that's where Joe first played. Is that right to Dreamland?
No. Wait a minute. Where did he open in Chappelle? I think, no, Joe Oliver opened at the Royal Garden. I thought it was in the Royal Garden. The Royal Garden. What? He opened at the Royal Gardens.
Well, I think he played first at the Deluxe one of them. Even before Royal Gardens.
I don't think he ever played in the Deluxe. I don't remember. No? No.
Fredy Cap is the one who played at the Deluxe.
Did you ever go to Deluxe? Sure. That's where I went to see Sydney Bessie. Oh. That's where I went to get that. I got that pawn ticket.
That was at the Deluxe, huh?
Yeah.
That's where Tubby Hall worked. That's where mine worked.

Uh-huh. Didn't the Royal Gardens have a balcony around inside? Yes. So, like little boxes or something like that? No. It was kind of old, curved, or something like that. Well, yeah, but they wouldn't call it boxes. It wasn't just a straight thing, though. No. Didn't it have sort of loops in it or something? Yes, it did. Little posts underneath to hold it up, or not?
Oh, yeah. Well, they've had posts, yeah. In them days, you know, they used to put a lot of posts in place.
But it was the dreamland that had that big light on the floor, huh?
Yes. When the people got up to dance or the floor show was going, they lighted up. And they had a glass floor. What was the point of that?
Did it look funny or something? No, it was just a novelty. Novelty?
